a CRASH at any phase before `verified` leaves a journal the next run rolls back

a second transaction waits for recovery, a concurrent edit is never rolled over, and unknown bytes refuse recovery

a declaration records the path, HEAD's blob and HEAD in the checkout's own git directory, and touches neither the tree nor the index
the declaration records the IGNORED COPIES the guard would pair it with, at declare time — the machine-local excludes included
a deletion staged with git rm can be declared; a file still on disk cannot (not even an in-place untracking): a declaration names a file that is GONE
NO WILDCARD, NO FOLDER, ONE SPELLING: each refusal is typed and records nothing
the shared HEAD reader answers exactly the paths asked: a folder asked with its own file is still a folder, and no sibling is added
an unborn branch has nothing to delete; outside a repository the refusal is typed
THE ONE STATE RULE: pending, mismatched, stale, expired, consumed; and the guard's verdicts
BOUND TO HEAD'S MOVES: a reset --soft back to the declared commit leaves the declaration stale for good; declaring again re-binds it
a declaration whose file came back is EXPIRED, and the next change to the record drops it (never waits for an accident)
a committed deletion is consumed and the record goes; an unused declaration stays, stale, and is re-bound only by declaring again
a checkout with no declarations is consumed by the lock-free reader alone: no state folder, no lock file
a declaration whose file changed in a commit is mismatched
a torn record and a record copied from another git directory are typed refusals; clear withdraws either
BOUND TO ITS INDEX: a linked worktree's declarations live in its own git directory and never reach the main checkout
the CLI's paths are taken literally: arguments, one path per line of each --paths-file, one per NUL of each --paths-file-nul, and anything after --
the status verb fails for any declaration that is not pending (stale, mismatched, expired), and passes otherwise
ONE WRITER AT A TIME: twelve declares in parallel processes all land in the record
ONE WRITER AT A TIME: a clear racing parallel declares never brings back what it reported withdrawn
a declared fix explains a suspect ONLY with its recorded reproduction, and only failures that measured the parent's bytes AND said what the reproduction saw
THE TEST FILE'S OWN BYTES COUNT: a failure that measured an edited test with the cause's old bytes is not the reproduced failure

THE TEST FILE IS HELD WHOLE: a failure that measured ANY other bytes of the test's own file — a sibling's edit, a parameterized or decoy title around it — is not the reproduced failure; no parse decides which bytes it measured (security T-1/T-2, correctness F-N1, design F4/F5)

WHERE IT FAILED COUNTS BESIDE WHAT IT SAID: a failure is the reproduced one only when its location is among the reproduction's for that digest; a row with no location matches only a reproduction whose failures named none (design NH-D)

A RECURRENCE VOIDS THE FIX FOR EVERY TEST IT EXPLAINS: one fix declared for two tests with one digest; a failure of either with that digest on bytes other than the parent's leaves BOTH red (design NH-D)
A FIX OF A CAUSE CHANGES THE CAUSE: a commit that edits only the test and names an untouched cause explains nothing, even with a record
THE TEST FILE MAY BE ITS OWN CAUSE, but only by a SEMANTIC change: a comment or layout edit is refused by name; a changed AST with its reproduction explains
A CAUSE NO READER JUDGES never counts as a semantic change: a fix that changed only such a cause explains nothing, and says which reader is missing
A STATISTICAL REPRODUCTION explains only at the configured N, with counts a no-op fix would show at most α of the time, and parent failures that said what the ledger row said
A RECORD THAT SHOWS NOTHING IS REFUSED BY ITS SCHEMA: zero parent failures, a fix run that failed, a statistical record with nothing alongside
A MOVED TEST clears only by a RECORDED MOVE into the live suite's manifest, never by absence
a cause the fix ADDED was absent where the failure ran: an absent path never keys equal
a cause the LATEST tree no longer holds is other bytes: a fixed suspect stays explained after its cause file is deleted
TWO CAUSES, TWO REPRODUCED FIXES: each failure is explained by its own fix's bytes and digest, never by the other's
A LATER DECLARATION (`@ <commit>`) resolves to the fix's full name; a malformed trailer or an unknown commit in history is REPORTED AND IGNORED, never thrown
THE COMMIT-MSG DOOR judges every Flake-cause trailer's syntax (an empty segment, an escaping path, no cause, a bad commit), and passes a good one
a Flake-cause value parses to the test's own path first, then its causes; the test's own file may be a declared cause, said once
THE SHIPPED commit-msg HOOK refuses a malformed Flake-cause trailer and passes a good one (the door, driven as git drives it)

a test that FAILED on the parent EVERY run and PASSED on the fix every run is recorded with its digest, the attempt is LOGGED with every run's output kept — and the record then explains its ledger failures
ONE RUN PER SIDE is strong only for a deterministic SHIM (--preload); without one a single run is refused — and the refusal is LOGGED like a record
a test that PASSED on the parent, FAILED on the fix, DID NOT RUN, or did not fail EVERY run of a deterministic reproduction is refused — nothing is recorded, the attempt is logged
A RUN THAT ENDS THE ATTEMPT EARLY is logged, every test refused with why, and the error still reaches the caller
A SKIP ROW THAT MERELY VANISHED ON THE FIX IS REFUSED: absence is not a pass (a moved test is recorded by `harness flake move`)

A STATISTICAL REPRODUCTION runs each side N times under the same conditions: STRONG counts are recorded with the loads; weak ones are refused with the runs their rate needs (the 1-in-N lottery is gone); zero parent failures, or one fix failure, records nothing
THE NO-OP PROBABILITY is the one-sided Fisher exact probability, and the runs a rate needs follow from it
A FIX THAT CHANGED NO DECLARED CAUSE'S MEANING runs nothing: an untouched cause, and the test file's own comment or layout edit, are refused by name
A MOVE is recorded only when the inventories show it: on the hermetic suite at the parent, gone at the commit, its destination a live suite file
the request: a door-owned variable is refused, a credential is REDACTED in the record (UR-21) but reaches the run, every flag is required, an unknown flag is refused

a record counts ONLY when an attempt the door kept recorded exactly its bytes: one the schema refuses, one filed under another key, one written by hand, one edited after, one from before the log are reported and explain nothing; an edited attempt is refused alone
R3-2: TWO BRANCHES' ATTEMPTS ARE TWO FILES — their merge is the union and breaks nothing; an id two attempts claim proves neither
S0: A SHIM NEVER REMOVES AN UNCONFINED PLACE — refused at the request, before anything runs
S0: EVERY RUN GETS A FRESH WORLD under the temp root, and a planted override failure is refused before any shim runs
EVERY LOOK COUNTS (design 8a, F-L2): a (test, fix) re-attempted is judged at α over its attempts — the refused ones included — so attempting until one passes never inflates the claim's error
every kept attempt is a text file that ends with its newline, named by the sha256 of exactly those bytes (the candidate format a checkout certifies; round 13)
a look is every attempt the door wrote: one a later schema refuses is refused as a record but still counted as a look (every look counts)

two heavy runs serialize: the second WAITS (never fails, never runs beside), naming the holder; it takes the lock once the first is gone
a run INSIDE a hold borrows it — whatever the holder's label holds (a backslash, a TAB, a long command): nesting reads the record's structured fields, never its label
a door killed outright never frees the lock under its command: the supervisor it ran the command under is adopted, and the next run waits until that whole process tree is gone
a light run takes nothing; what is heavy is config — a file is one, a folder or pattern is heavy, a path that names nothing is none, no argument is the whole suite

the stamp is READ from the live holder AND bound to its acquisition token: a run outside every hold is unslotted, whatever its environment says; a hand-written record naming this process stamps nothing; a dead holder's record stamps nothing
A HOLDER LABEL IS SHOWN ESCAPED AND BOUNDED, whoever wrote the record: no terminal escape, no forged second line

A HOLD IS BORROWED ONLY THROUGH A LIVE IDENTITY (security L-3): an adopted entry naming an ancestor's pid under another start time — an ended process whose pid was recycled into this lineage — lends nothing; the same entry under the real start time does
A RECORD'S ACQUISITION INSTANT IS AN INSTANT (security L-2): a forged line or a terminal escape in it makes the record unreadable, never a line on the waiter's screen
THE LOCK IS THE HOST'S, not the HOME's: its place comes from the password database's home and config; $HOME and $XDG_CACHE_HOME never move it; it stays under that cache folder

THE SUPERVISING DOOR (`harness slot run`, the coverage run, the perf profile) holds the lock while its command runs — the command, under the adopted supervisor, reads "held" — bounds its label to the program and argument count, and exits with the command's code; a signal-ended command exits 128 + its number. On a lock of the test's own: the host's lock is never a test's (correctness L-N3)
A WAITING DOOR HONOURS SIGTERM AND SIGINT (design L-1): the wait is asynchronous, a signal ends it with a typed exit (128 + its number), and the door never goes on to take the lock
NESTING READS ADOPTED PROCESSES TOO (correctness M2): a run whose ancestor is a process the holder ADOPTED (a supervisor it runs a command under) borrows the hold; one outside it does not
THE ANCESTOR'S STAMP NEEDS ITS TOKEN (correctness M3): inside an ancestor's hold, "held" only with the acquisition token the holder exported; without it, unslotted
THE LOCK'S PLACE IS REFUSED INSIDE A CHECKOUT (correctness M6): a lock path under the per-user cache that lies in (or around) the checkout is misplaced
A GRACE OF 0 IS SIGKILL AT ONCE (correctness M17): a target that ignores SIGTERM is killed, not asked
the CLI's exit for an interrupted wait is decided BY TYPE: 128 + the signal for the lock's own error, nothing for a look-alike (design LOW 14)
watchLauncher fires once the launcher exits, with the launcher's pid, and never while it lives
a recorded command is stopped with SIGTERM when its stop signal aborts — also when it aborted before the start — and the observation completes

IN-PROCESS: the installer the worker and the web setup call hands the guard the consented live hosts — and nothing without consent
the runner's preload hands the guard the declared live hosts only when the run's environment consents (exactly "1")
WIRING: every process that runs tests is guarded — the engine worker (after arming), each engine test file's process, each web worker
a supervised command's detached grandchild does not survive it, and its fd-3 report is passed through
a STOP reaches the command first (SIGTERM, within the grace), then the run ends as stopped
the recorded command (the engine worker's launch) runs supervised: the observation holds, and nothing it started survives
a receipt is CHECKED: a malformed or truncated last line is an absent receipt, never a cast
runBoundedTestProcess is ITSELF bounded: a supervisor that never closes (a holder keeps its pipes) is refused within the ceiling plus two graces
the run is EXIT-BACKED: a supervisor that exits while a holder keeps its pipes settles within the grace, unverified and with its output marked incomplete
the recorded command marks its pipes INCOMPLETE when the supervised output did not end (the observation never claims bytes it did not see end)
a stop requested BEFORE the supervisor announced its command still reaches the command as SIGTERM (never a supervisor killed before it held its signals)

the grace is the CALLER's (the suite watchdog's killGraceMs): a command that ignores its stop is killed when that grace ends
DRIVEN: a runner that DIES (SIGKILL) stops its supervisor (the parent-death signal): the command gets its grace, and nothing outlives the runner
the runner's death is ONE stop: its parent-death signal repeated (a dying multi-threaded runner reparents once per thread) never cuts the command's grace (PROMO01-SUPERVISOR-PDEATH)
after the runner's death, a REAL second stop still kills at once
